 Where is Caroline Ellison now? She's out of prison and landed a nonprofit job

 Caroline Ellison was not in charge of FTX when the cryptocurrency exchange publicly collapsed , but she quickly became a main character in the scandal — especially when she took the stand to point the finger at her on-again, off-again boyfriend, Sam Bankman-Fried.
 Ellison, the former CEO of FTX's sister company Alameda Research , is portrayed by Emmy-winning actor Julia Garner in Netflix's "The Altruists," a limited series that dramatizes Ellison's romantic relationship with FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried (Anthony Boyle) and the spectacular corporate meltdown that led Ellison to testify in Bankman-Fried's 2023 criminal trial in Manhattan federal court.
 Previously viewed as an altruistic wunderkind, Bankman-Fried was accused of stealing billions of dollars in FTX customer funds. Ellison's insider information about FTX and Alameda — as well as her diary entries and blog posts , which became public before and during the trial — are central to the public's understanding of Bankman-Fried's fall from grace.
 During her three-day marathon of testimony, Ellison told the jury that Bankman-Fried directed her to deceive Alameda lenders into believing both of his companies had more money than they really did. She also gave insight into Bankman-Fried's "risk-neutral" approach to business , his multi-million-dollar political donations , and his "distant" behavior as her boyfriend .
 "There was a feeling that I wanted more in our relationship," Ellison testified. "The whole time we were dating, he was also my boss, so that created some awkward situations."
 Jane Rosenberg's sketch of Caroline Ellison on the stand. 
 Jane Rosenberg/Reuters
 For his part, Bankman-Fried testified that he was "historically bad" at long-term commitments. "I didn't have the time or energy to put into what she wanted in the relationship," he said on the witness stand.
 Bankman-Fried was convicted on seven counts of fraud and conspiracy and sentenced to 25 years in prison.
 Meanwhile, Ellison struck a plea deal with the Justice Department, as did FTX executives Gary Wang and Nishad Singh . US District Judge Lewis Kaplan cited her "very, very substantial cooperation" with prosecutors and "genuine remorse" when handing down Ellison's two-year prison sentence in 2024.
 "You're a very strong person in some ways. But you're not inviolable. Somehow, for some reason — it's hard for me to understand — Mr. Bankman-Fried had your kryptonite," Kaplan told Ellison in court. "You were vulnerable and you were exploited."

 Ellison began her prison sentence on November 7, 2024 at the low-security Danbury Federal Correctional Institution in Connecticut.
 Ellison was released from prison in early 2026 and quickly landed a new job at a nonprofit
 Caroline Ellison outside the Manhattan federal courthouse on October 12, 2023. 
 Stephanie Keith/Bloomberg via Getty Images
 Weeks after Ellison reported to prison, nearly four months were shaved off her sentence , moving her scheduled release date up to July 20, 2026.
 Later, Ellison's sentence was further lightened. On October 16, 2025, Ellison was transferred into community confinement, which means home confinement or a halfway house.
 On January 21, 2026, at 32 years old, Ellison was officially released from the custody of the Federal Bureau of Prisons after about 14 months.
 For her first few months as a free woman, Ellison kept a low profile — but in July, she secretly landed a new job.
 Austin Chen, the founder and CEO of Manifund, announced on Substack in September that he had hired Ellison to help research "how to effectively direct philanthropic dollars."
 "I believe in redemption," Chen wrote. "Caroline has admitted her faults, worked to make creditors whole, and served her time in prison. I'd like to give her the opportunity to contribute back to the world; I hope that the world will concur."
 Manifund is a nonprofit previously backed by FTX Future Fund, a philanthropic initiative. According to Chen's post, Ellison started a "work trial" on July 13, 2026, before converting to full-time about one month later. He confirmed the news to Business Insider, but did not provide documentation of her employment.
 Chen's blog post also contained a message in Ellison's name.
 "I'm deeply sorry for what I did, and I completely understand why people may not want to work with me," it said. "But I'm very grateful to Austin for giving me a second chance, and judging me on my current work performance rather than my past. I feel very lucky not only to have a job, but to be working somewhere that I think is doing great work and has a mission I believe in."
 Ellison described some of her responsibilities at Manifund as "improving our technical infrastructure, working on operations and customer support, and posting updates on our newsletter."
 She added: "I probably won't reply to comments on this post—sorry."
